ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is a cyclohexene skeleton, with a C=C double bond inside the ring; the upper right side of the ring is connected to an exocyclic/external-ring C=C=N fragment; the lower right side of the ring is connected to a cyano-containing side chain, whose terminus is C≡N. On the right side are also shown two independent ethoxy-related fragments: one is negatively charged EtO⁻, and the other is neutral H-OEt. The curved arrows in the figure are ignored according to the problem statement. Then reason: the main organic fragment can be written as a cyclohexene with one intraring double bond, and bearing a cyanoethyl substituent and an exocyclic C=C=N fragment, corresponding to the SMILES N#CCC1CC=CCC1C=C=N. Neutral H-OEt is ethanol, with SMILES CCO; negatively charged EtO⁻ is ethoxide anion, with SMILES CC[O-]. The three disconnected components are connected with dots, giving CCO.CC[O-].N#CCC1CC=CCC1C=C=N.

method.method_draft: First read the visual structure only, ignoring the curved arrows. Transcribe the organic fragment as a cyclohexene ring with one C=C in the ring, a cyanoethyl substituent ending in N#C, and an exocyclic C=C=N group, yielding N#CCC1CC=CCC1C=C=N. Then encode the two ethoxy-derived fragments separately: neutral H-OEt as ethanol CCO and negatively charged OEt as ethoxide CC[O-]. Combine the disconnected components with dot separators to obtain CCO.CC[O-].N#CCC1CC=CCC1C=C=N.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中左侧是一个环己烯骨架，环内有一个 C=C 双键；环右侧上方连着一个外消旋/外环的 C=C=N 片段；环右侧下方连着一个含氰基的侧链，末端为 C≡N。右侧还显示两个独立的乙氧基相关片段：一个是带负电的 EtO⁻，另一个是中性的 H-OEt。图中的弯箭头按题意忽略。

再推理：有机主片段可写成带一个环内双键的环己烯，并带有 cyanoethyl 取代基和外环 C=C=N 片段，对应 SMILES 为 N#CCC1CC=CCC1C=C=N。中性 H-OEt 是乙醇，SMILES 为 CCO；带负电的 EtO⁻ 是乙氧负离子，SMILES 为 CC[O-]。三个不相连组分用点号连接，得到 CCO.CC[O-].N#CCC1CC=CCC1C=C=N。

planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the three disconnected species: a substituted cyclohexene bearing an exocyclic ketenimine/imino allene group (C=C=N-H) and a cyanoethyl/nitrile side chain; an ethoxide anion shown as OEt with a negative charge on oxygen; and an ethanol molecule shown as H-OEt. Also note the ring double bond and the nitrile triple bond, while disregarding all electron-flow arrows and the dot marking the transition state.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text instruction to know that the task is to choose/write the SMILES for the transition-state structure and specifically to ignore the arrows, so electron-pushing annotations should not affect the molecular graph.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard skeletal-structure-to-SMILES conventions: unlabeled vertices are carbons with implicit hydrogens; OEt means ethoxy/ethyl oxygen fragment; a circled minus on O gives [O-]; disconnected species are separated by dots; double and triple bonds are encoded with = and #; ring closures are numbered.
